scope: Recording project decisions: what a decision record carries (context, rationale, alternatives, decider, date, status, consequences), when to write one, where to keep it so it is findable, linking it to the work it affects, and supersession (a later decision that changes an earlier one acknowledges and links it). Covers ADR practice (Nygard, MADR, Y-statements, adr-tools, log4brains), cloud and government owners' ADR guidance (AWS, Microsoft, Google Cloud, GOV.UK), proposal processes that record decisions (Python PEPs, IETF RFCs, Rust RFCs), tracker linking (GitHub, Jira, Linear) and project frameworks (Scrum Guide, Kanban Guide). Not covered: datastore-selection's must-record-the-store-and-its-justification (cited, not restated) and linking between project records in general (project-record-linking); only supersession links are this topic's.
research_type: How-to / troubleshooting (LOW-MEDIUM bar: broad independent consensus); the one adoption figure is held to the Statistical bar and reported as a single study

questions.text: Best practices: what is current best practice for this topic?
Known solutions: what solutions, patterns, libraries and tools already exist, and how do they compare?
Platform guidelines: what do the platform owners' own guidelines say, for each platform the topic touches (Apple, Android, Windows, web, the databases and runtimes concerned)?
The expert's view: if we hired an expert consultant in this topic, what would they tell us: what to do, what to avoid, and what people usually get wrong?

methodology.method: guidelines/researching/process/research-methodology-and-sources: orient, go to authoritative sources (the originating article, cloud and government owners' ADR guidance, the template projects' own repositories, standards bodies' process documents, tracker vendors' docs), chain citations, corroborate across independent publishers, record provenance at generation time.
methodology.search_strategy: WebSearch on the topic only (architecture decision record best practice, supersede, template, decision log, decision tracking in PMBOK/PRINCE2/Scrum); WebFetch of each candidate page; every quote then re-checked verbatim against the page text with curl, except AWS Prescriptive Guidance, whose quotes come from the fetched page's markdown. One empirical study was located through the OpenAlex index and read there as its abstract.
methodology.inclusion: Primary sources first: the originator of the ADR (Nygard), owner guidance from AWS, Microsoft, Google Cloud, GOV.UK/GDS, the MADR, adr-tools and log4brains repositories, PEP 1, RFC 7322, the Rust RFC template, Atlassian, GitHub and Jira docs, the Scrum and Kanban Guides. Secondary expert sources (Fowler, Zimmermann, Thoughtworks Radar, Spotify Engineering, the Design Practice Repository, the Henderson ADR collection) only for the expert's view and what no primary source covers.
methodology.exclusion: Pages that could not be fetched as text (PMI 'On the Record', ProjectManagement.com Decision Tracker, AWS Architecture Blog ADR post, most of Linear's docs); paywalled standards (PMBOK, ISO 21502, ISO 31000) with no owner summary; exam-prep sites restating PRINCE2; vendor marketing without guidance.
methodology.scoring: Trust 0-100 = Authority 30 + Independent corroboration 25 + Accuracy 20 + Currency 10 + Transparency 15, per verification-and-trust-scoring. multi-independent only where two or more independent publishers hold the quoted words.

summary: All six rules hold. Context, rationale and consequences are the minimum every owner names (AWS, Microsoft, GOV.UK, Nygard). Alternatives are recorded by Microsoft, Google Cloud, MADR, Rust RFCs and PEPs, and Fowler and Zimmermann urge it, though Nygard's original template and the GOV.UK template omit them, so the sources support SHOULD rather than MUST. The decider is named by MADR (optional metadata), PEP-Delegate, DACI's Approver and GOV.UK's decision-level table; Nygard has no decider field, so SHOULD. Findability and linking to work are supported by Microsoft, GDS, Google Cloud, Thoughtworks and MADR, with GitHub and Jira supplying the link mechanisms. Acknowledging a changed decision is the strongest consensus: accepted records are immutable and a new record supersedes the old, linked both ways (Microsoft, AWS, GDS 'must', Fowler, Nygard, PEP 'must', RFC 7322). New practices with support: immutable-then-supersede, supersession links in both directions, a status lifecycle, a decision date, good and bad consequences, one short decision per record, only significant decisions, recording rejected proposals, confidence level, backfilling undocumented decisions, and no dummy alternatives. Scrum and Kanban Guides define no decision record; PMBOK, ISO 21502 and PRINCE2 primary texts were not reachable.
open_questions: Whether naming the decider is a MUST or a SHOULD: MADR marks decision-makers optional and Nygard's template has no decider field, while PEP-Delegate, DACI and GOV.UK always name one; the owner sets the strength.

Whether alternatives are required on every record, or only where two or more options were real: Nygard and GOV.UK omit the section, Google Cloud ties ADRs to 'two or more engineering options', MADR's minimal template keeps it.

Whether a clarification may edit an accepted record in place (GDS Way allows it before implementation; Henderson's collection prefers dated amendments) or every change must be a new superseding record (Microsoft, AWS, Fowler).

Where records live: in the code repository (Nygard, Fowler, GDS, Thoughtworks, log4brains) or a wiki readable by non-developers (Google Cloud notes both; Atlassian's decision log); or the repository with a mirrored wiki.
Which template to standardise on: Nygard's, MADR, or Y-statements; Zimmermann advises choosing one and sticking to it.

Whether 'deprecated' is a status distinct from 'superseded' (Nygard and MADR list both) and whether superseded records may ever be deleted (Zimmermann mentions deleting; Nygard and Microsoft keep them).
Whether sequential numbering is required (Nygard, Fowler, adr-tools) or avoided to dodge merge conflicts (log4brains).
limitations: PMBOK Guide, ISO 21502 and ISO 31000 are paywalled and no owner summary of their decision-log guidance was fetched; their position is not established.
PRINCE2's decision recording (issue register, project log) was found only in exam-prep secondary pages, not from AXELOS or PeopleCert; it is not cited.
SAFe and LeSS were not established: no fetchable owner page addressed decision records.
PMI's 'On the Record' article returned 403, ProjectManagement.com's Decision Tracker is premium, the AWS Architecture Blog ADR post and most of Linear's docs render only through JavaScript.
Linear's issue relations are cited from the page heading alone; Linear's full list of relation types was not readable.
AWS Prescriptive Guidance quotes were taken from the fetched page's markdown rather than a curl text check.
The adoption study (Buchgeher et al., IEEE Access 2023) was read as its abstract through OpenAlex; its figures are one mining study of public GitHub repositories and are not corroborated.
No study measures whether recording alternatives or deciders improves outcomes; the support is consensus guidance, not evidence of effect.
Apple, Android and Windows publish no guidance on decision records; the topic has no bearing on those platforms.
